risks.risk: Console may have hardware issues (disc drive failure, overheating, or unstable performance) that photos cannot reveal.
risks.proof: Short video of the PS4 powering on, reaching the home screen, and running a game for 10–15 minutes (showing no shutdown/overheat warning).
risks.if_unproven: Price as a used PS4 with unknown functionality (worst case: not fully working).

risks.risk: Ports may be faulty (HDMI/USB/Ethernet), which affects usability and resale value.
risks.proof: Photo/video close-ups of all ports plus a test showing HDMI output and at least two USB devices working.
risks.if_unproven: Price as if ports may be unreliable (worst case: some ports not working).

risks.risk: Controller may have drift/button issues or may not be the exact “double pad” set claimed.
risks.proof: Video showing controller connected and working: button presses, analog movement, and no drift in a simple calibration screen.
risks.if_unproven: Price as if controller condition is uncertain (worst case: controller needs repair/replacement).

risks.risk: Claim of “never opened or repaired” can’t be verified; internal repairs could exist.
risks.proof: Clear photos of the underside/model label and any warranty/void stickers, plus a photo of the screw heads (showing whether opened).
risks.if_unproven: Price as if repair history is unknown (worst case: previously opened/serviced).

risks.risk: Receipt/ownership proof is not shown; could be missing or not genuine.
risks.proof: Photo of the UK receipt (with sensitive details blurred) and matching serial/model label photo.
risks.if_unproven: Price without receipt/ownership proof (worst case: no valid proof).

proof_requests: Power-on video to home screen + 10–15 minutes gameplay (or system stress test) to confirm no overheating/shutdown.
Close-up photos of all ports (HDMI, USB, Ethernet, power) and a quick test showing they work.
Photo of the console underside/model/serial label (to confirm exact PS4 model and region).
Controller test video (buttons + analog movement/no drift).
Photo of the claimed UK receipt and a matching serial/model label.
response.reason: The item identity as a PS4 fat is plausible from photo 0, but the key value drivers (working status, ports, overheating, and receipt/never-opened claim) are not verifiable remotely from the single image. To price safely, we need functional proof and port/controller tests.
